name: Universal Design Workbench
purpose: Reusable knowledge base for product-grade UI, dashboards, admin tools, AI design studios, canvas editors, websites, motion, 3D/WebGL, component systems, proof/data integrity, and final visual QA.

handoffModes.auto: Inspect target files and choose forgestudio, dashboard, scratch, or universal.
handoffModes.universal: General product UI, dashboard, editor, app, or site improvement.
handoffModes.forgestudio: ForgeStudio-like AI design app, canvas editor, proposal/diff, verification, ledger, export.
handoffModes.dashboard: Dashboard, admin panel, records UI, data tool, or operations surface.

skills.name: product-ui-design-orchestrator
skills.useFor: Routing product UI work across runbook, IA, interactions, copy/status, decision/review, implementation slice, components, and QA.

skills.name: product-design-taste
skills.useFor: Taste and craft decisions for dashboards, SaaS apps, AI studios, canvas editors, data tools, and product websites.

skills.name: design-ai-workbench-screens
skills.useFor: ForgeStudio-like AI design workbench screens, proposal/diff review, verification, ledger, export, and canvas workflows.

skills.name: product-ui-component-sourcing
skills.useFor: Choosing local primitives, headless components, focused libraries, or catalog components without demo-data or landing bias.

skills.name: product-ui-visual-qa
skills.useFor: Final browser/screenshot QA, responsive/no-overlap review, state/copy/decision checks, accessibility, proof/data integrity, and verdict.

nonNegotiables: Do not force landing-page structure onto dashboards, editors, admin panels, data tools, or AI workbenches.

Working briefs must pass substance checks before coding: user/job/object, product object model, visual system contract, workflow/action path, data/source truth, route/screen, closest product surface blueprint, screen recipe/state specs, local files to inspect/change, component state plan, verification evidence, and top-design target.
Do not pass isolated decorative component work as a product slice.
Final implementation-slice reporting must preserve the working brief's route/screen, primary object, workflow/actions, data/source truth, and states.
Final reports must include visual-system evidence naming typography/type scale, spacing/density rhythm, surfaces/radius/borders, color/status/contrast, and target-local tokens/components.
Final reports must include information architecture evidence naming route/screen map, navigation/app shell, main/context zones, and responsive/recovery behavior.
Final reports must include interaction evidence naming primary actions/transitions, pending-success-failure states, recovery/permission behavior, and affected object/control.
Final reports must include copy/status language evidence naming affected object, state/status, reason or next action, and evidence/source/sample label.
Final reports must include decision/review cockpit evidence naming decision question, options/comparison, evidence/risk, action, after-state, and audit/recovery path.
Final reports must include component-state evidence naming changed components/controls, checked states, and screenshot/browser/manual/keyboard/responsive proof.
Do not fake metrics, proof, screenshots, imported assets, agent status, or completed work.
AI-design-app work must expose the trusted vertical: project, design search, import, object comment/task, proposal, preview/diff, verification, approval, transaction, ledger, export/reopen.
External AI output remains proposal-only until preview/diff, verification, approval, transaction, and ledger evidence exist.

AI design app working briefs must fill AI Design App Invariants before coding: proposal-only, preview/diff, verification, human approval, transaction/ledger evidence, agent connection/scopes, comment-to-task bridge, pending proposal/approval bridge, failure/recovery handling, and export/reopen recovery.

AI design app final reports must prove the operational pattern in `Operational pattern checked`, including agent connection/scopes, comment-to-task bridge, pending proposal/approval bridge, failure/recovery handling, and export/reopen recovery, not only show attractive panels.
Top-design handoff must pass the five-second test: primary object, state, risk, next action, recovery, and evidence are visible without reading implementation notes.
Final handoff needs real commands, screenshots/browser checks, or an explicit remaining-risk note.
